messages:
SRE-Bot: ALERT: etcd leader election spike detected in cluster-prod-usw2 (leader_changes=6 in 5m)
Mira Patel: seeing apiserver 503s at the same time, kube-scheduler logs show "failed to schedule pod" spiking for GPU pool nodes
Raj Singh: confirmed — some control-plane components report high request latency, controller-manager leader lease renewals delayed
Kevin Huang: any network flaps? I see a few packet drops from the us-west-2 fabric around 12:41 UTC in CNI metrics
Olga Novikova: also noticed one etcd member (etcd-2) has high disk latency on nvme, maybe IO contention from backups?
Mira Patel: timeline: 12:38 UTC leader change, 12:39 apiserver 503s, 12:40 scheduler backpressure, 12:44 lots of pending GPU pods with FailedScheduling
Raj Singh: for immediate mitigation we should: 1) cordon GPU nodes hitting schedule errors 2) scale up dedicated GPU pool in another AZ 3) restart apiserver on the flapping nodes if they still show 503s
Kevin Huang: agree. I'll cordon the affected GPU nodes now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-*-usw2a`
Mira Patel: thanks. I'm going to check etcd health: `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table` and grab member logs
SRE-Bot: NOTE: alert routed to #oncall and created incident INC-2304
Olga Novikova: etcd-2 logs show repeated WARN: "slow disk io" and periodic compaction spikes, looks correlated with S3 snapshot job at 12:36
Raj Singh: can we pause scheduled etcd backups? If snapshots coincide with peak traffic they destabilize leader election on small clusters
Mira Patel: pausing snapshots for now. Also bumping etcd election timeout to 5s from 2s is a quick config change we can try on the control plane bootstrap flags
Kevin Huang: caution — changing election timeout requires rolling restart of etcd members and tests. Could help reduce flapping but adds risk during change window
Olga Novikova: alternative: move older etcd member off noisy host (etcd-2) to a cleaner storage node; we have a spare on tag=fast-nvme
Raj Singh: short plan: A) pause snapshots, B) cordon GPU nodes and scale GPU capacity in usw2b, C) migrate etcd-2 to spare node, D) restart apiserver on control-plane nodes after etcd stabilizes
Mira Patel: executing A now. Raj/Kevin can you handle B and C? I'll monitor apiserver once etcd stabilizes and coordinate restarts
Kevin Huang: B done — cordoned 3 nodes and triggered scale-up in usw2b (requesting 6 additional GPUs).
Raj Singh: C in progress — snapshotting etcd-2 member state and starting migration VM; will update when DNS migrates
SRE-Bot: UPDATE: incident INC-2304 state=investigating, severity=high
Olga Novikova: after pausing snapshots, etcd leader changes dropped to 0 in last 2m. disk latency on etcd-2 still elevated but trending down after moving background IO off
Mira Patel: apiserver 503s dropped to almost zero. Scheduler backlog decreasing, GPU pods are transitioning to Pending->ContainerCreating in usw2b
Kevin Huang: reminder: a lot of these GPU nodes are spot instances — cost saving but makes capacity brittle. We should document a gated fallback to on-demand for control-plane heavy windows
Raj Singh: agreed. Postmortem action items: - move scheduled snapshots outside prod traffic windows - add monitoring for etcd disk io per-member - add automated migration to spare host when disk latency > threshold - consider increasing controller-manager leader-election retries
Mira Patel: also add runbook step: if leader_changes > 3/5m AND apiserver 5xx rate > 1% then escalate to SRE lead and consider immediate etcd member migration
Olga Novikova: capturing logs and perf data into INC-2304. I'll open PR for runbook changes and the snapshot schedule tweak
Mira Patel: thanks team — once etcd migration finishes and we validate stability we'll uncordon nodes and scale down the temporary capacity. Leaving incident open until 1h stable
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: transitioned to mitigated, monitoring for 60m stability window
Kevin Huang: uncordoned gpu-node-3 after validating kubelet/stress metrics; two pods replaced successfully
Raj Singh: etcd-2 migrated, cluster reports healthy: `etcdctl endpoint health --cluster` returns healthy
Mira Patel: closing notes: root cause = snapshot job + noisy host IO causing leader election churn -> apiserver timeouts -> scheduler backlog on spot GPU fleet. Mitigation = pause snapshots + migrate member + temp capacity shift. Follow-ups: move snapshots, add IO alarms, revisit spot policy for GPU pools.
Olga Novikova: adding cost note: 6 extra on-demand GPUs for 40min = estimated $1200. Logged to INC-2304 for chargeback.
Mira Patel: thanks all. I'll start the postmortem doc and link to runbook PR. :thumbsup:
